rules.late-read: the answer's sentence hidden from the last tokens in every attention layer (every layer on attention-only models) leaves <= 20% right with the Wilson upper bound <= 30%; the off-path sentence hidden there keeps >= 90% (lower bound >= 85%); on a hybrid, hidden in every DeltaNet layer instead keeps >= 90%. Memory -> prompt, items right unedited (fixed 22 Oct; scripts/d2_formats.py late_read)
rules.late-read-v2: reported beside late-read, whose verdicts do not change (Dan, 23 Oct). Memory -> prompt, items right unedited. The last tokens' share of the drop = (unedited - the answer's sentence hidden from the last tokens) / (unedited - hidden from every token after it); the relay = the first block's share right minus the second's. Holds iff the share >= 0.70, hidden from every token after it leaves <= 10% right with the Wilson upper bound <= 15% (the floor), the off-path sentence hidden at the same places keeps >= 90% at both, and on a hybrid the answer's sentence hidden in every DeltaNet layer instead keeps >= 90%. The last tokens are blocked as in late-read (every attention layer on a hybrid, every layer otherwise); every token after the sentence in every attention layer where the run has that block, else in all layers: the first scene set's runs blocked it in all layers, DeltaNet included, which on a hybrid hides more than the definition, so their share is a conservative lower bound (Dan, 23 Oct). A failed off-path control or a floor above its bar is not interpretable; a share below 0.70 fails, as does a DeltaNet block that keeps < 90% (as in late-read). The share's 95% interval: items resampled with replacement (paired), 4000 draws, seed 0 (scripts/cross_model_grid.py late_read_v2)
rules.name-digit: the off-path sentence's parts hidden keep >= 90% at both places (valid-split); then the sentence without its name hidden from the last tokens leaves <= 35% right and without its digit >= 70% (H-digit-final-split). Memory -> prompt (amended 22 Oct 16:40; scripts/d2_parts.py verdicts)
rules.formats: the late-read and name-vs-digit rules per format (prose, table, JSON), memory -> prompt (scripts/d2_formats.py, fixed 22 Oct evening)
rules.order-identity: A: 1st-2nd asked, position - identity, entity-cluster lower bound > 0; B: 3rd on, identity - position >= 0 with lower bound >= -0.05; holds iff A and B. Layer: the last swept layer where the donor's digit has its Wilson upper bound < 10%, or fixed (Qwen3.6-27B: 50) (scripts/finding5_confirm.py)
rules.counting: filler moved: the order slot's lower bound above the same place's upper bound, pooled and in >= 2 of 3 topics at one decisive layer; one more / one fewer: from the start above from the end and the same place, both layouts, same layer (scripts/pointer_swap.py v4x_tests). Decisive layers: the 27B's 48 and 50 and OLMo's 17-19 fixed; elsewhere the swept layers where the donor's digit has its Wilson upper bound < 10% (the specs)
rules.lens-gate-v1: the bridge in the lens's top 10 at its own sentence on >= 50% of items, the other bridge on <= 20% (scripts/lens_gate.py gate, 22 Oct)
rules.lens-gate-v2: the same bars read after the bridge's word (scripts/lens_gate.py gate_v2, 22 Oct 23:00)
rules.stated-bridge: at the cell chosen without the lens: the lens-readable part alone switches <= 10% of lookups and the rest >= 50%, while the lens-readable part switches >= 30% of recalls (the control); where set, lookups keep their answer under the lens-part patch on >= 80% (scripts/d1_verdict.py)
rules.push-main: rule v2: the valid cell with the most recall; holds (H-around) iff the lookup switches <= 10% and the scene-paired recall - lookup gap's lower bound >= 20 points; inconclusive where the rule says so (no control failed there); not interpretable when the off-path check fails or no cell writes recall (scripts/early_push_where.py decide)

rules.natural-read: the run's own verdict (scripts/natural_read.py verdict: the newest analysis-*-verdict/verdict.json): SQuAD paragraphs, items right unedited; the answer's sentence hidden from the last tokens leaves <= 10% right with the Wilson upper bound <= 20% (primary bar, Dan 23 Oct); finding 4's controls (another sentence hidden >= 90%, lower bound >= 85%; on a hybrid the DeltaNet layers instead >= 90%); the floor (hidden from every token after it) <= 10% or not interpretable; < 100 items not testable. rules.absent-entity: the run's own verdict (scripts/absent_entity.py, B4, fixed before the run): memory -> prompt decisive, named -> prompt reported; D = mean(1[order] - 1[fallback]) over the decisive items (k_d 2-5, original not asking its 1st), entity-cluster bootstrap 95% interval; 'order' iff D's lower bound > 0 and > the random push's upper bound (shown as holds), 'fallback' mirrored (fails), 'neither' (inconclusive). Per k_d rows: D on that k_d's decisive items, reported (the verdict is the pooled D)
rules.necessity: scripts/d1_verdict.py --rule necessity (B1, Dan 23 Oct 15:30): F(x) = share of items switched by pasting x; per cell lookups' J not needed iff F(full) - F(not_jspace) <= 0.10 where F(full) >= 0.50, recalls' J needed iff the drop >= 0.20 and above the random slice's drop (paired bootstrap lower bound > 0); a cell holds iff both, a set iff a majority of its cells, the model iff every set ('does not hold' shown as fails). The grid shows per cell and family the J-dependence (F(full) - F(not_jspace)) / F(full) and beside it the random slice's (F(full) - F(not_rand_sub)) / F(full): computed here from the verdict's rates, no interval. rules.rest-size: scripts/d1_verdict.py --rule rest-size (A2, Dan 23 Oct): at the decisive cell, the rest of the change shrunk to the lens part's norm (not_jspace_matched); H-size iff it switches lookups with the Wilson upper bound <= 0.10 (shown as holds), H-form iff its lower bound >= 0.20 with the lens part's upper bound <= 0.05 (fails), otherwise inconclusive
rules.late-switch: scripts/d1_verdict.py --rule late-switch (Dan 23 Oct ~12:00, 122B): the late switch holds iff at some decisive cell the lens part switches lookups with the Wilson upper bound <= 0.05, the rest >= 0.30, the recall control (lens part >= 0.30 of recalls) and the random-subspace control pass and it stays quiet later; finding 2 fails iff the lens part moves >= 20% of lookups (lower bound) at every decisive cell above rand_sub; otherwise inconclusive (the run's verdict, read as it is)
